To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the EFT action can be non-polynomial, (2) runaway solutions are not a problem for EFTs in general, and (3) the EBT can be time-dependent.

(1) the lowenergy effective field theory for a system with a time-dependent background can contain higher-derivative operators, even if the full theory is second-order, and (2) the EFT is valid as long as its predictions agree with those of the full theory to the order of interest.

the EFT is a valid description of the low-energy theory only in situations where (1) it is a valid effective theory, (2) the EFT action has the form required for the low-energy theory to have second-order field equations, and (3) the EFT solutions are stable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question “Who you gonna call?” when you need an effective field theory.
the question of what the EFT can tell us about the UV theory, and we conclude that in the presence of time-dependence the answer is: sometimes a great deal, but not always.
the following question: what are the conditions under which an EFT can be used to make reliable predictions?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EFTs are not always reliable, and the domain of their applicability should not be assumed a priori.
the EFT is valid for the range of energies for which its predictions are in agreement with those of the UV completion.
the domain of validity of a given EFT is determined by the extent to which it captures the dynamics of the underlying UV theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EFT is valid as long as the UV theory has a stable ground state and as long as the low-energy action can be derived from a UV action by integrating out the heavy degrees of freedom.
the domain of validity of an EFT is determined by the size of the couplings and not by the size of time derivatives in the equations of motion.
the EFT is a good description of the low-energy theory if the time dependence is sufficiently weak.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EFT is typically a good approximation for a wide range of physical situations, even if it does not take the form of an EFT in the traditional sense.

, when considering time-dependent EFTs, the EFT action should be viewed as a tool for understanding the dynamics of the theory, rather than as an object that is directly derived from a more fundamental theory.
the EFT need not have the same time-dependence as the UV theory, but rather the EFT must be valid for all times in order to be useful.
